title: Critique: epiphenomenalism makes knowledge of one's own mind, and of the view itself, impossible

statements.text: The strongest objection is that epiphenomenalism is incompatible with knowledge of one's own mind, and so with knowing that it is true. If a pain does not cause the utterance "I am in terrible pain", the same utterance would be made without the pain, and every argument for epiphenomenalism could be given by zombies with no mental life at all.

sources.quote: The most powerful reason for rejecting epiphenomenalism is the view that it is incompatible with knowledge of our own minds
even if we were all possessed of physical causes of our utterances and completely devoid of any mental life whatsoever
